name: Laberinto de Tilde
source: OSM: Entrambasaguas hamlet (Notion area); the maze itself is not in OSM
description: An outdoor hedge maze in Campoo, best combined with another outing in the area rather than a dedicated drive.
hours: Published opening 10:00–20:00; subject to weather. Check before travel.

name: Laberinto de Villapresente
source: OSM: Laberinto de Villapresente
description: A seasonal outdoor hedge maze near Santillana del Mar, easy to combine with a visit to the town.
hours: 2026: 28 Mar–12 Oct. Jul/Aug daily; rest closed Mon/Tue. Generally 10:30–20:00; last entry 19:00, earlier from 16 Sep.
booking: No reservation normally needed. Outdoor hedge maze; no umbrellas inside.

open.seasonNote: Open 28 Mar–12 Oct in 2026: Wed–Sun, daily in July and August

name: Parque de la Naturaleza de Cabárceno
source: OSM: Parque de la Naturaleza de Cabárceno
description: A large wildlife park in a former open-cast mine landscape near Santander. A full-day outing, with an annual pass worth considering.
hours: Year-round except 24, 25 & 31 Dec and 1 Jan; seasonal hours.
booking: 2026 tickets: adult €25/€35/€45; child 4–12 €15/€20/€25 depending on season. Annual Tarjeta Amigo: individual €80; family €170; Family Plus €200.

name: Zoo de Santillana
source: OSM: Zoológico de Santillana del Mar
description: A zoo just outside Santillana del Mar; a half-day outing that pairs with the town and its museums.
hours: Open every day from 09:30; official site currently states until 20:00 / dusk.
booking: Tickets at the zoo or online; check the current day tariff. Annual Club de Amigos: child 4–12 €50; adult €100; family up to 3 children €300.

name: Camaleño
source: OSM: Camaleño municipality centre
description: The Liébana municipality at the foot of the Picos de Europa; it includes Fuente Dé. A day-trip idea in your Notion.

name: Mirador de Covalruyo
source: OSM: Mirador de Covalruyo
description: A viewpoint above the Asón valley in Soba, saved in Notion as a hiking/family idea.

name: Sendero adaptado del Río Bayones
source: OSM: Sendero Adaptado del Río Bayones (path)
why: Very short family nature walk with ten tactile interpretation panels about local flora and fauna.

hike.childSuitability: Very suitable: short, low-difficulty adapted nature trail; part of the route is conditioned/protected with a handrail.

name: Rasines — Ruta Verde: Parque Paleolítico, La Balsa y Cantera Arqueológica
source: OSM: Rasines municipality centre (no start in Notion)
why: Signed local route through Rasines linking the Parque Paleolítico, La Balsa and Cantera Arqueológica.

name: Rasines — Ruta Azul: Balconada de Cerreo
source: OSM: Rasines municipality centre (no start in Notion)
why: Signed local Rasines route to the Balconada de Cerreo.

name: Ermita de San Esteban (Monte Corona)
source: OSM: Ermita de San Esteban
description: A small hermitage on a high point of Monte Corona (about 250 m) inside the Oyambre Natural Park. Next to it are a picnic area with tables and barbecues and a small viewpoint over the forest and the western Cantabrian coast; on clear days you can see San Vicente de la Barquera and the Picos de Europa. Reached by a paved forest road from La Hayuela. A pilgrimage (romeria) is held here around 3 August.

name: Colegiata de Santa Juliana
source: OSM: Colegiata de Santillana del Mar
description: Romanesque collegiate church from the 12th century, the heart of Santillana del Mar. Listed in the Cantabria Costa Central visitor leaflet.

name: Museo de Altamira
source: OSM: Museo Nacional y Centro de Investigación de Altamira
description: Museum and research centre for the Altamira cave art, with a permanent exhibition and activities for children and young people about how our ancestors lived. Listed in the Cantabria Costa Central visitor leaflet.

name: El Capricho de Gaudí
source: OSM: El Capricho de Gaudí
description: Small modernist villa by Antoni Gaudí from his first period (1883–85), with rounded forms, a tall tower and sunflower tile decoration. Listed in the Cantabria Costa Central visitor leaflet.

name: Cementerio modernista de Comillas
source: OSM: Cementerio de Comillas
description: Modernist cemetery on a hill facing the sea, set among the ruins of a former Gothic church and with an angel sculpture by Josep Llimona. Listed in the Cantabria Costa Central visitor leaflet.

name: Playa de Comillas
source: OSM: Playa de Comillas
description: Beach on the central coast. Listed in the Cantabria Costa Central visitor leaflet.

name: Playa de Luaña
source: OSM: Playa de Luaña
description: Beach on the central coast. Listed in the Cantabria Costa Central visitor leaflet.

name: Playa de la Concha
source: OSM: Playa de la Concha
description: Beach on the central coast. Listed in the Cantabria Costa Central visitor leaflet.

name: Playa de los Locos
source: OSM: Playa de los Locos
description: Beach on the central coast. Listed in the Cantabria Costa Central visitor leaflet.

name: Ermita de Santa Justa
source: OSM: Ermita de Santa Justa
description: Small cove with the hermitage of Santa Justa built into the rock; the start of the coastal route to Puerto Calderón. Listed in the Cantabria Costa Central visitor leaflet.

name: Monumento Natural de las Secuoyas del Monte Cabezón
source: OSM: Monumento Natural de las Secuoyas del Monte Cabezón
description: Natural monument of giant sequoias beside the CA-135 road between Cabezón de la Sal and Comillas; the trees can reach over 50 m. A pleasant short outing with a choice of walking routes. Listed in the Cantabria Costa Central visitor leaflet.

name: Casa de Leonor de la Vega
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: Built at the end of the 15th century and substantially remodelled in the 16th, this house is attributed to Leonor de la Vega, mother of the Marquis of Santillana, Íñigo López de Mendoza.

name: Casa de los Abades
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: Probably built at the end of the 17th century, this house originally belonged to the abbots of the Colegiata. Today it is known as the Casa de la Archiduquesa, having been the residence of Archduchess Margarita of Austria-Bourbon.

name: Casa de los Villa
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: A typical example of 18th-century town architecture, with pulpit-style balconies. In the mid-18th century it belonged to Francisco Antonio Pantaleón de Villa.

name: Casa del Duque de Almodóvar del Río
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: A magnificent 19th-century mansion, unique in Comillas because it is one of the few still owned by the original family, and it is still lived in: the owners spend their summer holidays there.

name: Centro Cultural El Espolón
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: Built in the late 18th century for Juan Domingo González de la Reguera, Archbishop of Lima and a native of Comillas, to house a Chair of Latin Grammar; the Real Seminario Cántabro was founded here in 1802.

name: Convento de San Ildefonso
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: Built in 1667 in Baroque style, this convent was richer in income and property than Regina Coeli, and its community often took in young women from the region's leading families and great lineages.

name: El Hombre de los Vientos
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: Also called "Alma de Costa", this bronze by sculptor Jesús González de la Vega was unveiled in October 2010. Standing on a stone pedestal, the three-metre statue shows a man meeting the sea wind with open arms.

name: Jardín Histórico de Puente San Miguel
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: Owned by the Botín family, this estate was declared a Site of Cultural Interest in the Historic Garden category in 1986.

name: Mirador Playa de la Tablía
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: This viewpoint stands above the beach of the same name, one of the wildest in Suances. It lies midway between Punta del Dichoso and Punta Ballota, with lovely views of the horizon and the cliffs.

name: Monumento al Marqués de Comillas
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: Raised by the town of Comillas in memory of Antonio López y López, who returned from Cuba, set up his businesses in Barcelona and was made Marquis of his native Comillas by Alfonso XII in 1878.

name: Museo de la Tortura
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: A museum displaying more than 70 European instruments of torture and capital punishment, from the Middle Ages to the industrial era. Dogs are allowed.

name: Museo Diocesano Regina Coeli
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: Housed in the former Dominican friary of Regina Coeli ("Queen of Heaven"), the museum holds over 800 works from parishes across the region, notable for their popular character and dominated by sculpture, which with stonemasonry was the region's traditional craft.

name: Museo Jesús Otero
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: Sculptor Jesús Otero Oreña left his legacy to his home town in this museum and foundation beside the Colegiata de Santa Juliana.

name: Palacio de Velarde
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: The finest example of Renaissance architecture in the town, built in the mid-16th century for Alonso de Velarde and also known as the Palacio de las Arenas. Its most important restoration was carried out in 1934.

name: Palacio de la familia Corro
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: This Renaissance palace, now the town hall of San Vicente de la Barquera, was commissioned in the 16th century by the inquisitor Antonio del Corro to shelter the town's sick poor.

name: Palacio de Peredo-Barreda
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: One of the town's most elegant and singular buildings, the ensemble comprises the palace, its annexed houses and their splendid garden.

name: Parque de la Ribera
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: A pretty park with impressive views over the Playa de la Ribera and the ría de San Martín.

name: Paseo por Novales y degustación de limonada
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: A stroll through this charming village, full of little channels. The walk is not complete without the obligatory lemonade or gin and tonic made with the area's prized lemons.

name: Playa de Covachos
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: A beach on the coast near Santander, about 3 km from Soto de la Marina, with a final stretch reached on foot.

name: Playa de San Juan de la Canal
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: A beach on the coast near Santander, 1 km from Soto de la Marina. It is well known for the busy party held nearby on the night of San Juan.

name: Puerto de Comillas (El Muelle)
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: Comillas men seem to have taken up fishing on a significant scale only in the 16th century, because San Vicente de la Barquera held the exclusive right to fish the coast for two leagues east and west of its harbour.

name: Ría de San Martín de la Arena
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: An estuary on Cantabria's central coast, between the municipalities of Suances, Polanco and Miengo, where the river Saja reaches the sea.

name: Ruta Cascadas de Toñanes
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: An easy walk that starts by the village of Toñanes, with just one tricky part: the final descent to the waterfall, which can be a little slippery for small children.

name: Torre de los Velarde
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: A Gothic tower built in the mid-15th century by García de Velarde, head of one of the town's great lineages. It was substantially remodelled in the early 17th century.

name: Torre del Merino
source: CANTUR / Turismo de Cantabria points of interest (official coordinates): https://cantur.net/santander/infoTools/views/gesPoi.php?idCat=64
description: A medieval Gothic tower of military character, built in the 14th century. It was the residence of the merino, the king's representative, after Santillana was made capital of the Asturias de Santillana in 1209, the largest jurisdiction in medieval Cantabria.
